dossier.purpose: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS (Noble Numbat) root-filesystem image for the Windows Subsystem for Linux, published on releases.ubuntu.com under a Canonical Ltd. copyright footer as ubuntu-24.04.5-wsl-amd64.wsl (371M, last modified 2026-09-08 00:19), next to SHA256SUMS and SHA256SUMS.gpg. The release page describes it as 'the root filesystem to be installed and launched by the Windows Subsystem for Linux'. Support dates for 24.04 LTS come from Canonical's release-cycle page: standard security maintenance to May 2029, ESM to May 2034, Legacy add-on to May 2039, with Ubuntu Pro-gated items flagged. The 'Ubuntu on WSL' docs hub links to the install, GPU/CUDA and Ubuntu Pro for WSL how-tos. Evidence basis: this is not a code repository. The working directory holds only .round-meta.json (read_at taken from .round-meta.json:11). Every fact therefore comes from the three listed pages, read through a fetch tool that returns processed text, not raw HTML. Citations are URLs with section or row labels, not line numbers. The listed docs URL answered 301 and redirected to https://ubuntu.com/wsl/docs/latest/, which I read as that page's content. No page outside the three listed ones was opened.

claims.claim: WSL image description: 'The WSL image is the root filesystem to be installed and launched by the Windows Subsystem for Linux.'

File index row: ubuntu-24.04.5-wsl-amd64.wsl, 371M, last modified 2026-09-08 00:19; companion ubuntu-24.04.5-wsl-amd64.manifest, 16K, 2026-09-08 00:19. Every file name in the index is an -amd64 build; no arm64 WSL file is listed.

claims.claim: SHA256SUMS (893 B) and SHA256SUMS.gpg (833 B), both last modified 2026-09-15 19:11, are published in the same index. The page presents no instructions or notes on checking downloads against them.

The page heading is 'Ubuntu 24.04.5.1 (Noble Numbat)' under the /24.04.5/ path. Only the desktop ISO is named 24.04.5.1 (5.8G, 2026-09-14 23:20). The server ISO (3.8G), netboot tarball (98M) and WSL image are named 24.04.5. The page does not explain 24.04.5 versus 24.04.5.1.
The same index still lists older WSL images: ubuntu-24.04.3-wsl-amd64.wsl (361M, 2025-08-05 17:00) and ubuntu-24.04.4-wsl-amd64.wsl (373M, 2026-02-10 01:01), each with a .manifest.
'LTS are released every two years and receive 5 years of standard security maintenance.'

Ubuntu 24.04 LTS 'Noble Numbat' row: 'Released: Apr 2024'; standard security maintenance May 2029; expanded security maintenance May 2034; break/bug support May 2034; legacy add-on May 2039; architectures amd64, armhf, arm64, s390x, riscv64, ppc64el-p9; upgrade path 24.10, 26.04 LTS.

'ESM extends the life of LTS releases by providing 10 years of security updates for the 'Main' repository and also adds 10 years of security coverage for the 'Universe' repository.' ESM is available through Ubuntu Pro. 'At the end of the 10 year ESM period, the Legacy add-on can be purchased to cover additional 5 years.'

Chart legend labels (as returned by the fetch tool): 'Standard Security Maintenance for packages in Main' carries no Pro tag. 'Expanded Security Maintenance for packages in Universe', 'Break fix and bug support' and 'Legacy add-on for security coverage and support' are each tagged Ubuntu Pro. The page does not state what Universe packages receive without Ubuntu Pro after year 5.

'Ubuntu Pro is Canonical's enhanced security and support subscription for Ubuntu systems.' 'Ubuntu Pro subscriptions are free for personal use on up to five machines.' It 'includes up to 15 years of security coverage (ESM and Legacy add-on), Kernel Livepatch, Landscape, FIPS 140-3 certified packages, and CIS hardening.'

Packages are grouped into 'Main' and 'Restricted' (the base system) and 'Universe' and 'Multiverse' (community and extra packages); 'Main' and 'Universe' are open source. Footers carry Canonical Ltd. copyright and trademark notices ('© 2025' on the release index, '© 2026' on the release-cycle page). No SPDX identifier or licence file appears.

Ubuntu on WSL 'enables developers to run a GNU/Linux environment on Windows'. Ubuntu Pro for WSL is 'a tool for managing Ubuntu on WSL' enabling 'automatic attachment of your Pro subscription to Ubuntu instances, and remote deployment with Landscape.'

The hub links the how-tos 'Install Ubuntu on WSL' (https://canonical-ubuntu-on-wsl.readthedocs-hosted.com/latest/howto/install-ubuntu-wsl2/), 'Enabling GPU acceleration with CUDA' (.../howto/gpu-cuda/) and 'Security overview for Ubuntu on WSL' (.../explanation/security-overview/). The hub itself has no text on supported Windows versions, the WSL 2 requirement, install methods, systemd, GPU/CUDA, Ubuntu releases offered, lifecycle, licence or telemetry. A keyword search of its links found none for NVIDIA, systemd, Windows 10/11, import, .wsl, release or versions.

risks: Version-label ambiguity: https://releases.ubuntu.com/24.04.5/ is headed 'Ubuntu 24.04.5.1 (Noble Numbat)' and its index mixes 24.04.3, 24.04.4, 24.04.5 and 24.04.5.1 files, including three .wsl images (24.04.3 at 361M, 24.04.4 at 373M, 24.04.5 at 371M). The page does not explain 24.04.5 versus 24.04.5.1, and no 24.04.5.1 WSL image is listed, so the image must be selected by exact file name.

The page has no verification instructions or key information, and the files were not opened. It is therefore unconfirmed that SHA256SUMS has a line for ubuntu-24.04.5-wsl-amd64.wsl or which key signed it.

Needs the listed pages do not cover: systemd user services, Python 3.13 / Node 24 / Rust versions, NVIDIA RTX 4090 access through WSL, compatibility with WSL 2.7.13 and kernel 6.18, and the install procedure. The docs hub says none of these appear on it and links install and GPU/CUDA how-tos that were not opened. Docs are spread across three hosts: documentation.ubuntu.com returns 301 to ubuntu.com/wsl/docs/latest/, whose links point to canonical-ubuntu-on-wsl.readthedocs-hosted.com, and the docs are labelled 'latest' (https://ubuntu.com/wsl/docs/latest/).

Toolchain currency is unknown: the release-cycle page lists 24.04 LTS as 'Released: Apr 2024' and names 26.04 LTS in its upgrade path (https://ubuntu.com/about/release-cycle). Neither the release page nor the docs hub publishes package versions, and the 16K manifest was not opened.

Security coverage is split by repository and by Ubuntu Pro. Standard maintenance covers 'Main' (to May 2029). The chart legend tags Universe ESM, break-fix/bug support and the Legacy add-on as Ubuntu Pro items. ESM runs to May 2034 and the Legacy add-on 'can be purchased' to May 2039. Pro is 'free for personal use on up to five machines' (terms page not opened). The page does not state what Universe packages receive without Pro, and no listed page says which repository the needed toolchain packages come from (https://ubuntu.com/about/release-cycle).

Image refresh cadence: the index shows WSL images dated 2025-08-05, 2026-02-10 and 2026-09-08, one per point release about 6-7 months apart, and no intermediate WSL image is listed (https://releases.ubuntu.com/24.04.5/). The pages do not describe how or when updates reach an installed image.

Licensing is undocumented on the listed pages: no SPDX identifier or licence file appears, only Canonical Ltd. copyright and trademark notices ('© 2025' on the release index, '© 2026' on the release-cycle page) and legal links that were not opened. The release-cycle page says 'Main' and 'Universe' are open source and says nothing of the kind for 'Restricted' and 'Multiverse'.

Evidence limits: there is no repository or source, so no code, tests, CI, SBOM or release-workflow evidence exists (working directory holds only .round-meta.json). Pages were read through a fetch tool that returns processed text; one request for a literal reproduction of the release index was declined, and the chart-legend wording for years 6-10 could not be reproduced consistently. The input 'repository' URL (https://ubuntu.com/download/server) is the server download page, not in pages_to_read, and was not opened.
